indicators.note: Half tells us to keep only the first half of the word minute, its opening three letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A timing quibble: something lasting thirty seconds or under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half a minute' looks like thirty seconds, but it means the first half of the word minute, MIN, followed by OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor describes something smaller or lesser in size or importance.

clue.text: Much time and trouble is taken in its drafting

definitions.text: Much time and trouble is taken in its drafting

parts.note: an age is a very long stretch of time

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters of the word and are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint about how long it takes to write up the programme for a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' looks like a noun beside 'Much time', but it is the anagram signal working on 'and'. The whole clue is also the definition: a meeting's list of business is notoriously laborious to draft.
explanation.definitionFit: The list of items for a meeting is drafted beforehand, often with considerable effort.

clue.text: Back one aiming to retain his title

definitions.meaning: in football and other team sports a back is a player in a defensive position

definitions.text: one aiming to retain his title
definitions.meaning: a champion putting a title on the line in a contest is said to be defending it

explanation.surface: A sports report about a champion back in the ring to keep a belt.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport the word covers both a rearguard player and a reigning champion facing a challenger.

clue.text: Voting against, told to go and vote for

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
someone told to go has been sent away

explanation.surface: A muddled voter who opposes, is dismissed, and then supports.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent is to agree to or approve a proposal, as a vote in favour does.

parts.note: a person who wholeheartedly indulges in festivities and celebration, wallowing read as revelling

explanation.surface: A partygoer happily immersed in festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who revels takes part in lively celebration, enjoying it to the full.

clue.text: City Jane Eyre came to love

definitions.meaning: a cathedral city in Kent, England
in Charlotte Bronte's novel the heroine falls for her employer

explanation.surface: A literary note on where a famous heroine found romance.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a Kent cathedral city and to the master of Thornfield in Bronte's novel.

clue.text: The only one in a suit wearing a vest

definitions.text: The only one in a suit

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest
clothes you are wearing are on you

explanation.surface: A man in a business suit with an undershirt beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' is the card-game sense: in bridge a lone card held in a suit has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games a holding of just one card in a suit is called by this name.

definitions.meaning: a large jib sail on a yacht
Christopher Columbus was born and grew up in this Italian port

explanation.surface: Seafaring history: where a famous explorer set sail or grew up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a big foresail and the Ligurian port city that was Columbus's birthplace.

clue.text: Getting married in a church will be a high spot

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for married inside the letters for church

parts.note: CE is short for the Church of England
M is the abbreviation for married in records

explanation.surface: A church wedding is promised as the highlight of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the peak or highest point of something.

parts.note: club doormen who throw people out, punning on cheques that are returned unpaid

explanation.surface: Who throws out worthless cheques?
explanation.definitionFit: Doormen who eject troublemakers share their name with cheques that come back unpaid.

indicators.note: soundly signals that the word is heard rather than read, so a word for examines is said aloud

parts.note: to examine something is to check it, so examines means checks

explanation.surface: A doctor thoroughly examining patients from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Czechs are people of the Czech Republic in central Europe.

definitions.meaning: a group of musicians playing together

explanation.surface: A bare pairing of two words, music and circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a group of players and a ring or loop.

parts.note: to needle someone is to goad or provoke them
the SS began as Hitler's personal protection unit

explanation.surface: Provoking a Nazi guard would be pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means not required, uncalled for.

parts.note: old means from an early time
a bailey is the defensive wall or courtyard of a castle

explanation.surface: A lawyer's early argument for the defence in a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defence' suggests a barrister, but it is the castle-wall sense. The Old Bailey is London's Central Criminal Court.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Central Criminal Court is known by this name.

indicators.note: the clue simply says the letters of the preceding words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crossword-setter's reminder that a clue may end or be an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A closure is a finish or conclusion.

clue.text: Drug could have bearings on the case

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: S and E are compass bearings, south and east
the dative is a grammatical case

explanation.surface: A detective's medicine might affect how a case turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks legal, but it is the grammar sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative is a calming drug.

parts.note: a spar is a pole, as on a ship's rigging
red is the traditional term for a communist

explanation.surface: A Pole and a Communist came to blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it is the timber sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers who sparred traded practice blows with each other.

indicators.note: a turn here is a twist given to the letters, rearranging those of a pierrot

explanation.surface: A clown's performance in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is South Africa's administrative capital.

definitions.meaning: the scope or extent of something

explanation.surface: A rambler's kit: a range of hills and something to navigate by.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both scope or extent and the navigator's magnetic needle instrument.

parts.note: the last named of three men in the Book of Daniel thrown into the furnace and emerging unburnt

explanation.surface: An insurance term: fire cover for a third party.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests insurance policies; in fact it is the Bible story of Shadrach, Meshach and a third companion surviving Nebuchadnezzar's furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the third of the three Hebrews who survived the fiery furnace unharmed.

indicators.note: deranged means put out of order, so the letters of Lear are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's mad king, losing his mind and his crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a king demoted a rank might become a nobleman of this title.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble below a king's rank is what a demoted monarch might become.

definitions.meaning: to have the ... is to have an advantage
the keenness or sharpness of a blade

explanation.surface: Enthusiasm gives you an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a slight advantage over rivals and the sharpness of a blade.

clue.text: Man in a boat helps the pilot

definitions.meaning: one of the three in Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat
RAF slang name for an aircraft's automatic pilot

explanation.surface: A crewman assists the boat's pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerome K. Jerome's novel Three Men in a Boat features George, Harris and J.; 'George' was also slang for an autopilot.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a character in Jerome's boating novel and to the old nickname for an autopilot.

clue.text: Provide a finale to the second half of the show

parts.note: a finale is the end of a performance

indicators.note: keep only the latter half of the word show, its final two letters

explanation.surface: Adding a grand closing number after the interval of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give or supply, especially funds or a quality.

clue.text: Vehicle it is illegal to leave in the street

definitions.meaning: a curtained couch carried on poles

definitions.text: it is illegal to leave in the street
definitions.meaning: rubbish dropped in public places, an offence in Britain

explanation.surface: A notice: no abandoning cars on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests illegal parking; the vehicle is the old carried couch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a carried couch and rubbish dropped in public.

clue.text: Crack discovered far below the surface

parts.note: a crack player is an expert, a pro
found means discovered

explanation.surface: A fissure was detected deep underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' suggests a fissure, but it is the adjective for an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound means very deep, literally or intellectually.

explanation.surface: Heading away on a vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to depart and authorised time away from work.

clue.text: I cast heavyweight in capital part

parts.note: to sling something is to cast or throw it
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A theatre director casting a big star in a leading role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' and 'part' suggest theatre; ISLINGTON is a borough of London, the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of London, the British capital, has this name.
